messages.subject: computing Rasch values within SEM using lavaan?
parts:
Hello all

i have a smallish data set (700 cases) and 40 items on a likert scale (1-5). i would like to run SEM on the items but would like the items to be on a Rasch scale.

i am able to compute said "Abilities" on a different software but when i "plug" this external values into the SEM, i am not taking account the error associated with said measures.

  

is there a way to do it all in Lavaan? 

let's say i have 8 items : I1-I8 which should represent 2 latent constructs (L1 and L2) that are first order factors and F1 which is a second level factor:

L1=~ I1+I2+I3+I4
L2=~ I5+I6+I7+I8
F1=~ L1+L2 (not sure if i should use =~ or just ~)

not sure how i compute Rasch values inside this model. 



 i am fairly new to Lavaan but i have a bit of a working knowledge in R

thank you all for helping!

messages.subject: Re: computing Rasch values within SEM using lavaan?
parts:
Your model is right.
However in SEM framework, You can ONLY using Graded Response Model what extended model of 2PLM.

And you may have to use 'wlsmv' estimator and 'ordered' arguments.

Seongtho Bae

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: computing Rasch values within SEM using lavaan?
parts:
On 09/20/2015 04:18 PM, isomitzi wrote:
> i have a smallish data set (700 cases) and 40 items on a likert scale
> (1-5). i would like to run SEM on the items but would like the items to
> be on a Rasch scale.

Strictly speaking, Rasch only deals with binary items. For ordinal
items, a popular method is the graded response model. Instead of a
single 'difficulty' parameter, you will get a set of 4 thresholds per
item. In addition, by default, lavaan will allow the factor loadings
(which can be converted to discrimination parameters) to be different
for each item. In the spirit of Rasch, you may want to force them to be
equal for all items.

> is there a way to do it all in Lavaan?
>
> let's say i have 8 items : I1-I8 which should represent 2 latent
> constructs (L1 and L2) that are first order factors and F1 which is a
> second level factor:
>
> L1=~ I1+I2+I3+I4
> L2=~ I5+I6+I7+I8
> F1=~ L1+L2 (not sure if i should use =~ or just ~)

The second order factor is not identified without further restrictions.
If you are using std.lv = TRUE, you should constrain one factor loading
to 1.0:

model <- '
L1 =~ I1 + I2 + I3 + I4
L2 =~ I5 + I6 + I7 + I8
F1 =~ 1*L1 + L2
'

fit <- cfa(model, data = ..., std.lv = TRUE, ordered = paste0("I",1:8))


If I1-I8 are ordinal, this will correspond with the graded response model.

If you wish to constrain the factor loadings to be equal (within each
latent variable), you need to use labels. Same labels imply same
parameter values:

model <- '
L1=~ a*I1 + a*I2 + a*I3 + a*I4
L2=~ b*I5 + b*I6 + b*I7 + b*I8
F1=~ 1*L1+L2
'

And of course, you can add regressions to this model...

Yves.
